content.text:
The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. It type-checks cleanly under `tsc --strict`, and `npm run size -- out/module.ts` prints 206 bytes (min+gzip) with 95 bytes of own code.

I couldn't compare against the original. Lodash isn't installed, so `src/module.ts` fails to build and type-check, and that is also why the baseline numbers are missing. I didn't run the equivalence check against the example inputs.

| lodash | es-toolkit | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `keyBy(rows, fn)` | `keyBy` | Same call shape. |
| `sumBy(rows, 'age')` | `sumBy(rows, (row) => row.age)` | The strict version takes only a function, not a property-name shorthand, so this is the small adapter. An empty array still gives 0. |
| `sortedUniq` | `uniq` | es-toolkit has no `sortedUniq`. For sorted input, `uniq` gives the same result, since duplicates are adjacent and first-occurrence order is kept. |

No lodash import remains. All three functions come from the main `es-toolkit` entry, so `es-toolkit/compat` isn't needed. The exported signatures, `Row` and `Config` are unchanged.

I made two assumptions about behaviour. For `byId`, the later row wins when ids repeat, as in lodash. The `uniq` swap is only equivalent because the input range guarantees ascending order.
